subject: Follow-up: Observability & runbook tests for Redwood vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Zhao <aaron@stratoai.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T16:04:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Observability & runbook tests for Redwood vs hyperscalers

Hi Aaron — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

1) Recap of what we heard from StratoAI: currently running Bedrock for inference, looking at cost predictability and production visibility (request tracing, model-level latency SLOs, token-cost attribution). You want a concise comparison vs your current hyperscaler setup and a short test run that proves parity or advantage for Redwood.

2) Suggested test matrix (what we can provide):
   - Baseline latency & p99 under steady-state traffic (Bedrock vs Redwood).
   - Tail latency + tracing: simulate artifact that produces cold KV cache, confirm tracing IDs propagated to your APM.
   - Token-level cost breakdown: token counts + unit cost per model variant and per-route dashboards.
   - Observability & alerting: show per-route SLOs, automatic regression alerts tied to prompt evals.
   - Failover behavior: run short capacity drop and confirm graceful fallback to cheaper model variant.

3) Runs & role ask: Redwood can stand up a short-lived test harness in our hosted environment. To move forward we need a contact (or a test account) from your infra team and the primary KPI thresholds you care about (p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens target, retention window for traces/logs).

I've attached an observability comparison PDF that maps feature-by-feature against the common hyperscalers and a rough timeline for a 3-day test. If this looks good, can we schedule the hands-on test the week of Feb 22?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-observability-matrix.pdf

From: Aaron Zhao <aaron@stratoai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Mercer <kyle@stratoai.com>
Date: 2026-02-13T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & runbook tests for Redwood vs hyperscalers

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the matrix. A few immediate items from our side: 

- Can you share example dashboards (Grafana/Datadog) for the token-level cost traces and the per-route latency breakdown? We currently use Grafana + Tempo and Datadog for APM.
- Are your traces OTLP-compatible? We need to ingest spans into our existing tracing pipeline and link them to request IDs.
- For retention: what's the default retention window for request traces and usage logs in hosted mode and in a Dedicated deployment?
- For the failover test: will Redwood provide an automated load script or do you want us to run the runner from our side?

We're also running a small eval on Vertex for a few endpoints so it'd be great to see the exact metrics you plan to expose. 

I'll loop in Kyle (infra) to coordinate our test credentials — Kyle, can you share an S3 bucket and a small sample workload (1000 requests, mixed prompt sizes) that we can use for the run?

Appreciate it, Aaron
Director of Platform Engineering
StratoAI
aaron@stratoai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Zhao <aaron@stratoai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & runbook tests for Redwood vs hyperscalers

Aaron — great questions. Short answers and what we'll deliver before the test window: 

- Dashboards: attaching a PNG export of our per-route dashboard (latency percentiles, token-cost heatmap, active model variant split). We can provide a Grafana JSON export or a Datadog dashboard template; let me know which you prefer.
- Tracing: Redwood supports OTLP natively and can export to your Tempo/Grafana stack. We propagate a request_id through the runtime and include model-variant, route, sequence_length, and cache-hit metadata on spans.
- Retention: hosted default is 30 days for traces/logs; Dedicated can be configured up to 90 days; Private deployments are customer-controlled. We also offer an archival export to S3.
- Load runner: Redwood will provide a containerized runner and a short script (JMeter wrapper) you can run from your network, or we can run it from our hosted harness — your choice.

Attached is a short runbook (redwood-test-plan-runbook.md) that outlines step-by-step what Redwood will perform vs what we ask StratoAI to provide. Proposed schedule:
  - Feb 22: test environment setup + credential exchange
  - Feb 23: steady-state latency & token-cost runs
  - Feb 24: failover + tracing correlation verification + final report

If that schedule works, can Kyle send the S3 bucket + a service account for the runner? Also, what's your target p99 and acceptable token cost or % delta vs Bedrock that you'd accept as a win?

—Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Zhao <aaron@stratoai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Kyle Mercer <kyle@stratoai.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & runbook tests for Redwood vs hyperscalers

Aaron / Kyle — looping in a short operational plan from our side so roles are clear before the 22nd: 

1) What Redwood will provide (owner: Redwood infra — Olga):
   - Grafana dashboard JSON + Datadog template for per-route SLOs and token-cost heatmaps (drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-strato-test-plan).
   - Containerized load runner and a small harness that emits OTLP spans with the request_id and model metadata attached.
   - A short post-test report comparing p50/p95/p99, average token cost per 1k tokens, and tracing correlation success rate.

2) What StratoAI will provide (owner: StratoAI infra — Kyle):
   - S3 bucket with sample prompts and a test credentials file for the runner.
   - A minimal traffic profile (1000 requests, mixed tokens) and the Bedrock/Vertex baseline metrics if available.

3) Acceptance criteria / KPIs:
   - p99 latency within 20% of your Bedrock baseline OR token-cost savings >= 10% (one or the other).
   - OTLP traces ingestable by your Tempo stack and request_id correlation > 95% for successful runs.

4) Timeline: confirm by EOD Feb 18. Test window Mar 22–24 (contingent on confirming access and credentials earlier).

Related: HubSpot record DEAL-9874 created and I've attached the observability matrix for internal reference.

If you confirm the S3 + credentials and the acceptance thresholds, we'll schedule the test harness. Happy to take a quick 15m sync next week to finalize details.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai
